For the second year in a row, the top three ranks of the Civil Services Examination, 2022, conducted by the Union Public Service Commission have been secured by women. In a spectacular achievement, results announced on Tuesday show that 12 women are in the top 20. The 26-year-old topper, Ishita Kishore, who graduated from Delhi University’s Sri Ram College of Commerce and is a resident of Greater Noida, reached the pinnacle in her third attempt. Thanking her family for their support, Ms. Kishore said she read up on current affairs and practised writing at length because the examination process can be draining. The second-rank holder, Garima Lohia, 24, from Buxar and is also a Delhi University graduate, cleared the examination in her second attempt; and Uma Harathi N., 28, who stood third, is an engineering graduate from Telangana and cleared it in her fifth attempt. The young women’s reflections on success and failure, the need to persevere against all odds and the importance of an empathetic ecosystem are significant pointers for future students, teachers and parents. However, Sundays had a special place in his heart. Sundays were the days when Ravi would watch his favorite superhero, Shaktimaan, on television, and later, engage in outdoor games with his friends. As soon as the rooster crowed, Ravi would spring out of bed and finish his chores quickly. He’d then rush to the old black-and-white TV set placed in the corner of the living room, eagerly waiting for his hero to appear on screen. With wide-eyed fascination, he would watch Shaktimaan fight the villains, thus standing up for justice and righteousness. Every episode would end with Shaktimaan delivering a moral message, which Ravi would ponder upon, long after the show had ended. Once the show was over, Ravi would step out into the bright sunlight, excited to share the day's episode with his friends and play his favorite outdoor games. The kids from the neighborhood would gather in the nearby playground, all eager to discuss Shaktimaan's latest feats and to recreate the scenes in their games. They would begin with Gulli-Danda, a game which required precision and agility. Ravi loved to be the striker, fantasizing himself as Shaktimaan striking down the forces of evil. As dusk descended, Ravi would return home, exhausted but filled with joy.
